findings.title: getBaseConditions returns an unparenthesized OR expression that is unsafe to compose
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` is meant to be dropped into a larger `WHERE` clause. When only the authorization condition is returned (line 75), it is returned bare. For org and team scope that is `(A) OR (B)`. A caller writing `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" > ${d}` gets `(A) OR (B) AND startTime > d`. Because AND binds tighter than OR, the date or other filters then apply only to the second branch, so team-booking rows are returned unfiltered. The combined branch wraps both sides in parentheses, but the single-condition branches do not. Always wrap the result, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, so the returned fragment is safe to compose.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions hide the real contract
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So `authConditions` is never falsy, and the `else if (filterConditions)` and `NOTHING_CONDITION` fallbacks can never run. The apparent "fail closed" fallback is unreachable and misleads readers about the invariants. Simplify to `filter ? sql\`(${auth}) AND (${filter})\` : sql\`(${auth})\``.

findings.title: Public findMany method removed without replacement or caller audit
findings.body: `findMany(args)` was the service's public entry point for fetching bookings. It is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing caller (tRPC handlers or other services) will fail to compile, or will have to build its own raw query. The PR description only talks about updating tests and does not mention this breaking change or confirm that no other callers exist.

findings.title: Constructor options type loosened, allowing scope 'team' without teamId at compile time
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` therefore type-checks. At runtime the zod discriminated-union validation fails, `this.options` becomes null, and the service silently returns `1=0`, so the caller sees no data and no error. The compile-time guarantee from the discriminated union is lost. Keep the strict type, or surface the validation failure.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted although caching behavior remains
findings.body: The "Caching" describe block was removed. The service still memoizes via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so the behavior is now untested. Nothing checks that a second call returns the cached value, or that a `null` filter result is cached rather than rebuilt. The tests should have been updated to the `Prisma.sql` expectations, not dropped.

findings.title: Only the user-scope SQL is executed against the database
findings.body: The conditions that matter most for security are the org and team scopes, with `= ANY(${array})` array binding and the nested `(...) OR (...)` grouping. These are only compared against hand-written `Prisma.sql` strings and never run against Postgres. The single `$queryRaw` test uses user scope with an eventTypeId filter. It never checks that another user's or another team's bookings are excluded, and never exercises array parameter binding or operator precedence. A syntax error or wrong grouping in the org or team SQL would pass the string-equality tests. Add DB-backed tests for team and org scope with a negative case, plus the empty-user-list team case.
